resolved_disagreements.positions: Evaluator instance 3 REFUTED it, measuring 1e1000000.toFixed(2) at 40 ms and linear. Security instance 3 CONFIRMED it as a BLOCK, measuring Money.format() at 4,152 ms for 1e100000 and non-completion in 100 s for 1e1000000.
resolved_disagreements.resolution: Security instance 3 is correct and evaluator 3 probed the wrong sink. The cost is not in toFixed but in the quadratic thousands-separator lookahead /\B(?=(\d{3})+(?!\d))/g at frontend/src/types/money.ts:78; security 3 explicitly measured toWire() as cheap (0.3 ms) to isolate the regex as the whole cost. This is the clearest single case in this gate where running three instances changed the outcome: the finding would have been recorded as refuted on a single-instance run.
resolved_disagreements.status: upheld as BLOCK (latent — no frontend entry point exists at HEAD)

resolved_disagreements.positions: Evaluator instance 3 measured a 9,708 ms blocking-CPU shape on the integer-scalar path. Security instance 3 REFUTED the DoS, measuring a 109 ms worst case for a 10-million-digit input with every pathological exponent rejected in under 0.1 ms.
resolved_disagreements.resolution: Not reconciled by shared evidence; the two instances probed different shapes and neither re-ran the other's. Both agree on the residual defect that matters: a bare decimal.Overflow escapes Money.multiply at money.py:101 because _quantize catches only InvalidOperation. Recorded as an open WARN with the timing claim marked disputed rather than silently resolving it in either direction.

resolved_disagreements.positions: Evaluator instance 2 filed F-2A (MAJOR): the two justifications in logging.py:217-223 are demonstrably false.
resolved_disagreements.resolution: Instance 2 proved it by counterfactual rather than argument — it re-enabled uvicorn.access two ways against the real production factory. Native emits plain text (so the AC3 hazard is real), but routing it through the JSON root handler — the treatment uvicorn.error already receives — yields valid JSON carrying the correct request_id, and preserves client address, HTTP version and query string. The claim that request_id_var is already reset is disproven empirically and against uvicorn source (httptools_impl.py:484 emits synchronously inside the middleware's await send(message)). AC3 passes on its merits; the comment misrepresents why, and disabled = True is broader than the problem.
resolved_disagreements.status: WARN — no contract failure, but the stated rationale is false and should be corrected rather than inherited by later stories

lockfile_not_versioned.method: git check-ignore -v frontend/package-lock.json; git ls-files | grep -i lock
lockfile_not_versioned.observed: .gitignore:48 (*.lock) and :49 (package-lock.json) ignore dependency lockfiles repo-wide, so NEITHER frontend/package-lock.json NOR backend/uv.lock is under version control, although both exist on disk. The patterns sit under a 'Generated / large files Claude should skip' comment, conflating 'do not read this large file' with 'do not version it'. No dependency pinning exists in VCS for either stack.

gate_integrity_findings.finding: The computational security scan reported a clean pass having scanned ZERO files. The /gate skill's documented invocation is `--all --staged --boundary-only`; the staging area was empty, so files=[] and runSastDetail returned {ran: true, hadTargets: false} — self-reporting as having run while emitting no skip warning for semgrep. Re-running with explicit file arguments correctly revealed that gitleaks, semgrep AND pip-audit are all absent from this environment. Separately, runDeps(cwd) only probes the repo ROOT for package.json; this project's only manifest is frontend/package.json, so npm audit was never invoked at all and its absence was never reported.
gate_integrity_findings.impact: security-scan.json with total:0, blocking:0 was vacuous on all three tiers. Manual npm audit found 5 vulnerabilities including 1 critical (vitest <=4.1.10, CVSS 9.8, GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp) and 1 high (vite <=6.4.2, CVSS 7.5, GHSA-fx2h-pf6j-xcff, a server.fs.deny bypass on Windows alternate paths — directly applicable on this win32 host). All three security instances independently downgraded these to WARN on the grounds that they are devDependency-only and @vitest/ui is never invoked, which is sound; the defect is that the gate's own sensor never measured them.
gate_integrity_findings.recommendation: Make runSastDetail distinguish 'no targets' from 'ran clean' in the report, and have runDeps discover manifests recursively rather than root-only.

gate_integrity_findings.finding: regression-suite-full BLOCKed with 54 findings, every one 'expected status N, got 0', across contracts A.json through M.json. discoverPriorContracts() treats every file in sprint-contracts/ as a prior baseline unless --exclude-group is passed, and the gate-checks registry passes none — so it graded 12 groups whose endpoints do not exist yet, against no running server.
gate_integrity_findings.resolution: Re-ran correctly against a live server. Group A's own contract: pass, 0 findings (specs/reviews/regression-gate-verdict-groupA-live.json). True baseline with all groups excluded: 'no prior contracts to re-validate' — correct, since groups_completed is empty and A is the first group. The regression axis is genuinely clean.
gate_integrity_findings.recommendation: The registry entry cannot know the current group. Either pass the current group through from the lane, or have the gate read groups_completed from claude-progress.txt.

gate_integrity_findings.finding: canvas-sync BLOCKed on a single entry: .claude/state/red-phase-presnap.json, a harness state file modified in the working tree. changedFiles() is `git diff --name-only HEAD` with no exclusion filter, so harness control-plane state is graded as design-governed product surface.
gate_integrity_findings.resolution: Re-ran scoped to the 13 production source files: 0 issues, fully synchronized (specs/reviews/canvas-sync-check-productscope.md). No product file is unsynced.
gate_integrity_findings.recommendation: Exclude .claude/state/** from the canvas-sync changed set.

gate_integrity_findings.finding: The script ignores --out and always writes specs/reviews/slo-verdict.json. The orchestrator's deliberately-poisoned probe therefore overwrote the canonical artifact with verdict:fail / error_rate_pct:99.9. Detected and repaired: the poisoned reading was preserved as slo-verdict-poisoned-evidence.json and slo-verdict.json was regenerated against a clean server (verdict:pass, error_rate_pct:0).
gate_integrity_findings.note: Consistent with the known harness pattern that pipeline scripts ignore unrecognised flags rather than rejecting them.

gate_integrity_findings.finding: As the ownership-check waiver itself records, run-gate-checks.js has no waiver-application path — waivers apply at pre-commit only. None of the four active waivers covers canvas-sync or regression-suite-full, so neither registry BLOCK was suppressed; both were resolved by scoped re-runs instead.

A concurrent security instance wrote 17 untracked backend/_probe_* scratch files (including a 29 MB log) mid-gate, which made `ruff check .` — the command in CLAUDE.md's quick reference — report 41-92 errors. Evaluator instances 1 and 2 both caught that the context pack's 'lint clean' claim did not reproduce, and both correctly localised it to untracked scratch rather than product code. The instance removed its own files on completion; the orchestrator re-verified afterwards: ruff check . / pytest / mypy all clean, 88 tests passing, product working tree pristine.
